---
title: "Getting started"
---

## Install

ggp-client needs Python 3.10 or later.

```bash
pip install "git+https://github.com/jossl95/ggp_client"
```

## Log in

Downloading needs the access link the portal emails you (request it on the portal's login page). The first
download asks you to paste it; the input is hidden. The session is then saved in `data/.session.json` (readable
only by you) and reused, so the link is needed once. ggp-client looks for a login in this order:

1. the saved session, if it still works;
2. the `access_url` argument of `ggpClient`;
3. otherwise it asks (input hidden). With no terminal to ask on (a scheduled job) it stops with a `LoginError`.

::: {.callout-warning}
The access link works like a password and is valid for seven days. Do not commit it, and use the prompt rather
than writing it into a script as `access_url`. ggp-client never writes it to its log.
:::

## A first script

```python
import asyncio
from ggp_client import ggpClient

async def main():
    async with ggpClient(project="ggs", round=2, country=["nl", "at"]) as p:
        await p.sync()                  # index the portal into data/catalogue.sqlite
        for r in p.rows:                # the files the filters select
            print(r["id"], r["series"], r["wave"], r["country"], r["version"], r["size_mb"])
        await p.download(ext="dta")     # Stata files only
        await p.preprocess()            # each data file to parquet + meta.json
        await p.consolidate()           # one dataset per round and wave

if __name__ == "__main__":  # needed: preprocessing runs in worker processes
    asyncio.run(main())
```

`ggpClient` is asynchronous: open it with `async with`, inside an `async def` that `asyncio.run` starts. Every step
is logged, with time stamps, to `data/ggp_client.log`; `data_dir="elsewhere"` puts the catalogue, the session, the
log and the downloads somewhere else.

## Index the portal

`await p.sync()` reads the public dataset pages, then logs in to add the Harmonized Histories and Additional
Datasets, which the portal lists only on the logged-in data access page. Without a login it indexes the rest and
reports what it skipped. It returns `(found, failed)`.

The catalogue is a SQLite database, open as `p.con`. `p.rows` holds the files that match the client's filters,
refreshed after `sync` and `download`; each row works like a dict, with `id`, `series`, `wave`, `country`,
`version`, `size_mb`, `local_path` and the other catalogue columns.

## Filters

The filters are arguments of `ggpClient`. Each takes one value, a list, or `None` (all). Case does not matter,
and a value that is not in the catalogue raises a `ValueError` instead of selecting nothing.

| argument | values |
|---|---|
| `project` | `"ggs"`, `"ffs"`, `"hh"` (Harmonized Histories), `"other"` (Additional Datasets), `"teaching"` |
| `round` | `1`, `2` (or `"i"`, `"ii"`) |
| `wave` | `"w1"`, `"w2"`, `"w3"`, `"pilot"`, ...; for `hh` and `other` the dataset name, e.g. `"nkps"` |
| `country` | two-letter codes: `"nl"`, `["nl", "at"]`, ... |
| `ids` | catalogue id ranges: `[(3, 12), (20, 20)]` |
| `all_versions` | `True`: also superseded versions (default: the latest only) |

Look at `p.rows` first: it shows what `download`, `preprocess` and `consolidate` will work on. Each of them also
takes `rows=` to work on other rows than the client's.

## Download

```python
async with ggpClient(project="ggs", round=2, wave="w1", country="nl") as p:
    await p.download()                    # data files only (dta, sav and csv), latest versions
    await p.download(ext=["dta", "sav"])  # only these types
    await p.download(metadata=True)       # also codebooks, readmes and other documents

async with ggpClient(project="ggs", round=2, force=True) as p:
    await p.download()                    # download again and overwrite
```

Each call returns `(done, skipped, failed)`. Archives (zip, and 7z for most GGS-I wave 1 files and the Harmonized
Histories) are unpacked into one folder per file, keeping their structure; an archive inside the archive becomes a
folder. Existing files are never overwritten, so your own changes survive; asking for more later (another `ext`,
or `metadata=True`) adds the missing files. A download with no matching file is reported as failed and leaves
nothing behind.

## Then

```python
async with ggpClient(project="ggs", round=2) as p:
    await p.preprocess()   # each data file to parquet + meta.json
    await p.consolidate()  # one dataset per round and wave
```

See the [GGS-II use case](ggs-ii.qmd) for what these produce, and the [reference](reference.qmd) for every
argument and for the same steps as `ggp-client` commands on the command line.
